newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks end off Wall St-led highs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks end off Wall St-led highs.

text.p: *Stocks close off highs after market is boosted by record levels hit on Wall Street on Friday. Turnover 259.06 million, value $601.36 million, 991 stocks traded, 312 steady, 428 up, 251 down

The Australian share market closed higher on Monday aided by the record set on Wall Street on Friday, but the local market was unable to hold all of the early gains, with brokers expecting a quiet week ahead.
At 4.10 p.m. (0610 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 15.5 points up at 2,267.8, almost matching Friday's 15.7 point increase, but off the morning high of 2,275.6.

The September share price index futures were 23 points up at 2274, holding a 6.2 premium to the underlying index after being at a discount for the past few trading sessions. Brokers said there were few fresh leads to keep the market at its highs.

"The market got a bit of a kick from the bonds, which opened quite strongly, but there was not much to go on with as the market is still a bit hesitant after some of these earnings downgrades," said broker Kevin Massey at ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
"It's a typical sort of quiet Monday as the market settles and waits on more confirmation on where interest rates are going," Massey said.

Wall Street soared to a record high on Friday on the back of fresh U.S. economic data that calmed higher interest rate fears. The U.S. policy-setting Federal Open Markets Committee (FOMC) next meets on September 24.
Massey said the market would be a bit "whippy" for the rest of the week as there was little significant local economic data this week. Any move is likely to come from offshore leads.
Mining and forestry group North topped turnover lists due to dividend related trading. Rises outnumbered falls by 1.7 to one.
The solid fuel and developers/contractors indices were the only sectors to go against the market trend.

In other local markets, Australian bond yields showed double digit falls across the curve following Friday's steep advance in U.S. Treasures. The key benchmark November 2006 bond traded around 8.0 percent for most of the session.
The Australian dollar was quiet after an offshore slide sundered support and soured sentiment on the currency. At 4.50 p.m. (0650 GMT), the local dollar was quoted at US$.7914/19.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivatives trade saw active trade although it was down on last week's busy levels.
